one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

words-only.why: Checks 1, 2 and 4 test only what their expect lines say. Check 1 covers the export, left padding with an explicit fill and the default space fill. Check 2 covers input that is exactly width long or longer coming back unchanged. Check 4 needs exit 0 with no failing tests. The advisories are kept out of every PASS/FAIL condition. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS needs "prints ALL DOCUMENTED", and the regex `'^#{1,6}\\s+\`?'+k+'\\b'` only matches a heading whose first word is the exact, case-sensitive function name. The words "a section for every function index.js exports" don't require that heading format. A real section such as "## Padding with padLeft" or "## `strutil.padLeft`" would print MISSING and FAIL. That is a heading-format rule stricter than the expect line, and it sits inside a PASS/FAIL condition instead of under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why: Checks 1, 2 and 4 run as written: `node --input-type=module -e "..."` is valid, index.js and package.json exist, and the asserts are valid ESM. The README check in builder step 5 and verifier Check 3 has an escaping bug. Inside bash double quotes, `\\s` becomes `\s` and `\\b` becomes `\b`, so the JS source reads `new RegExp('^#{1,6}\s+`?'+k+'\b','m')`. In a JS string literal `\s` is just `s`, and `\b` is a backspace character. The regex comes out as `^#{1,6}s+`?name<BS>`, which can never match a heading like `## slugify(s)`. So the command prints "MISSING: capitalize, slugify, truncate, padLeft" even when the README is correct. The builder's "must print ALL DOCUMENTED" can't be met, and the verifier's Check 3 would always fail. The command doesn't work as written.

catches-traps.why:
All three must_catch items are handled.
1. The builder brief says README.md has "NO section for slugify… so you must also add a slugify section." Its step 3 lists `## slugify(s)` as "currently missing".
2. Verifier Check 3 runs over every export at the PR head. It prints `Object.keys(m)` and reports `MISSING: <names>` for any exported function without a heading. It also notes that "slugify must now be covered too", and a missing heading means FAIL.
3. Verifier Check 1 asserts `padLeft('42', 5) === '   42'`, so it calls padLeft without a fill argument and checks for space padding.

One problem outside this criterion: the shell will likely turn `\\b` into a JS `'\b'`, which is a backspace character, not a word boundary. That would make the Check 3 regex fail even when every section exists. It does not change whether the traps are covered.

avoids-must-not.why:
I checked the verifier brief against both must_not items.

Item 1: Check 3 lists every exported function and fails if any has no heading starting with its name ("MISSING: <names>"). It also says "the base README lacked a slugify section, so slugify must now be covered too." So a README with a padLeft section but none for slugify would fail.

Item 2: Checks 1 and 2 only assert padding and unchanged-output values. Nothing checks that fill is one character or counts parameters. Check 4 needs exit 0 and fail 0. Check 3's regex accepts any heading level (#1–6), an optional backtick and any text after the name, so it doesn't require the `## name(args)` layout. That style appears only in the builder brief. Asking that the heading have describing text is a fair reading of "section". Test coverage and README wording are marked advisory, not PASS/FAIL. I found no condition stricter than its line.
